resolvedContracts.finding: Prompt requests largest to smallest; the ordered answer runs refinery gases to bitumen (smallest to largest). Preserved pending direction choice.
Note requests three fields. Literal answer has two semicolon-separated groups, with Heat included as a pipe alternative to sulphuric acid/H2SO4. Needs field-separator resolution.

Notes request four-choice MCQ plus conditional exception fields, but selected types vary. Q083 contains interface instructions in the answer box; Q084/Q085 use pipes between different exceptions rather than required separate fields. Preserve text until the shared response contract is specified.
Note requests splitting ionic/metallic answers, while selected type remains single-field and wording still combines both. Requires explicit two-field structure or two questions.
Changed to MCQ with a correct answer but no supplied distractors. Options still need authoring.
Answer uses Test:/Result: on separate lines instead of semicolon-separated fields; requires explicit mapping to the two-field contract.

styleFindings.finding: How do I test ... and what result would I get? alternates with How do you test ... and what is the positive result?
Substance names and answer colours alternate between title case, sentence case and lower case: Carbon Dioxide / oxygen gas; Orange-red flame / red flame; Orange to Green / green to black.
Definition prompts vary in colon use, Define a versus Define the term, final full stops and the phrase when talking about organic molecules.
Small quantities alternate between numerals (2, 3) and words (two, three).
Some prompts have no final punctuation; Q113 is phrased as a question but ends in a full stop. Answer separators have inconsistent surrounding spaces and Q084 has leading/trailing spaces.
Prompts alternate between sulphate and sulfate. Accepted alternatives also include both spellings; that allowance may be intentional.
Iron (III) / Copper (II) use a space before the oxidation state, while copper(II) does not.
Proton/electron prompts say relative charge; neutron prompt says charge.

Bromide still says dilute/aqueous and uses (aq); chloride and iodide use the simplified wording requested by the teacher. All retained exactly; this is a consistency observation, not a request to restore qualifiers.
Q046 uses 100oC, whereas numerical temperature items use a space and °C.

policy: Teacher source preserved; subsequent consistency fixes explicitly authorised by user.
